front.title: The Intent Token - A Credential for Delegated User Intent

abstract.t:
Autonomous Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents translate high-level, often ambiguous natural-language instructions from end users into multi-step chains of downstream API invocations. Traditional OAuth 2.0 authorization mechanisms bind access tokens to static, pre- configured scopes or fine-grained resource parameters known at the time of user consent, leaving a semantic gap when an agent dynamically determines exact execution parameters at runtime.
This document specifies the Intent Token, a cryptographically signed, sender-constrained JSON Web Token (JWT) profile that captures either user-approved authorization bounds or host-attested user instructions, together with an upper-bound authorization envelope and optional step-up action triggers. Rather than being presented directly to Resource Servers, an Intent Token serves as a verifiable input artifact at the Authorization Server or a dedicated Policy Decision Point (PDP) — either exchanged via OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) — optionally accompanied by a client-side Agent Delegation Proof (ADP) — for short-lived, narrowly scoped downstream access tokens, or submitted via Pushed Authorization Requests (RFC 9126) to establish or advance a stateful authorization workflow.
